## When to use

Use this skill whenever you are working with @mastra/core to obtain the domain-specific knowledge.

## How to use

Read the individual reference documents for detailed explanations and code examples.

### Docs

- [Code mode](references/docs-agents-code-mode.md) - Configure Mastra code mode so agents can run multi-tool computations in isolated local or remote sandboxes and return one accurate, consolidated response.
- [Guardrails](references/docs-agents-guardrails.md) - Protect Mastra agents with built-in guardrail processors for prompt injection, content moderation, PII redaction, Unicode normalization, and output safety.
- [Human-in-the-loop](references/docs-agents-human-in-the-loop.md) - Add human-in-the-loop controls to Mastra agents with tool approval and suspended execution, so people can provide input before a run resumes or stops.
- [Agent networks](references/docs-agents-networks.md) - Understand deprecated Mastra agent networks, including multi-agent routing, structured output, tool approvals, and migration to supervisor agents.
- [Agents](references/docs-agents-overview.md) - Build Mastra agents that use LLMs, tools, memory, workflows, and subagents to reason through open-ended tasks and return structured or streamed responses.
- [Processors](references/docs-agents-processors.md) - Use Mastra input and output processors to transform, validate, filter, and control agent messages at defined points in the execution pipeline.
- [Structured output](references/docs-agents-structured-output.md) - Generate validated, typed structured output from Mastra agents with JSON Schema, Zod, or Valibot, including streaming and tool-enabled responses.
- [Tools](references/docs-agents-tools.md) - Create schema-validated Mastra tools that let agents call APIs, query databases, run functions, and invoke agents, workflows, or remote MCP servers.
- [Composite Auth](references/docs-auth-composite-auth.md) - Combine multiple Mastra authentication providers with CompositeAuth, control provider order, and support fallback across JWT, OAuth, and custom identity systems.
- [Custom auth provider](references/docs-auth-custom-auth-provider.md) - Create a custom Mastra authentication provider by extending MastraAuthProvider, with token validation and user authorization protecting selected server routes.
- [Fine-Grained Authorization (FGA)](references/docs-auth-fga.md) - Configure Mastra Fine-Grained Authorization for resource-level permissions that map routes to actions and scope stored resources for enterprise users.
- [JSON Web Token](references/docs-auth-jwt.md) - Secure Mastra APIs with MastraJwtAuth and a shared secret, then create JSON Web Tokens and send authenticated requests through MastraClient.
- [Simple Auth](references/docs-auth-simple-auth.md) - Use Mastra SimpleAuth for token-to-user authentication, API key scenarios, custom headers, and lightweight authorization in development environments.
- [Workers](references/docs-auth-workers.md) - Secure communication between standalone Mastra workers and the API server with bearer tokens, API key headers, or custom authentication credentials.
- [Browser](references/docs-browser.md) - Give Mastra agents browser automation through native SDK providers, CLI tools, CDP connections, or cloud services such as Browserbase and Firecrawl.
- [Channels](references/docs-channels.md) - Connect Mastra agents to Slack, Discord, Telegram, and other messaging channels with webhooks, thread context, tool approvals, and formatted replies.
- [A2A (Agent-to-Agent)](references/docs-connections-a2a.md) - Expose Mastra agents through the Agent-to-Agent protocol and consume remote A2A agents as subagents or call them directly with the client SDK.
- [Agent Client Protocol (ACP)](references/docs-connections-acp.md) - Connect ACP-compatible coding agents to Mastra as tools or subagents, with configured models and sessions that stream Agent Client Protocol interactions.
- [Connections](references/docs-connections-overview.md) - Connect Mastra to remote agents, coding agents, SDK runtimes, MCP servers, and external tools by choosing the protocol that fits your application.
- [SDK agents](references/docs-connections-sdk-agents.md) - Use Claude Agent SDK, Cursor Agent SDK, and OpenAI Agents SDK agents inside Mastra as delegated agents with their native tools and model options.
- [Workers](references/docs-deployment-workers.md) - Run Mastra workflow orchestration, schedules, and long-running background tasks in dedicated workers to keep API processes responsive under load.
- [Develop](references/docs-develop.md) - Develop and test Mastra agents locally with mastra dev, Studio, file-based agents, the Mastra CLI, and AI coding tools that understand your project.
- [Custom scorers](references/docs-evals-custom-scorers.md) - Build custom Mastra scorers with createScorer using JavaScript functions or LLM prompts across preprocess, analyze, generateScore, and generateReason steps.
- [Datasets](references/docs-evals-datasets.md) - Create versioned Mastra datasets, define item schemas, manage test data through code or Studio, and track experiments against agents and workflows.
- [Evals with memory](references/docs-evals-evals-with-memory.md) - Run Mastra evals against memory-enabled agents using shared or per-item threads, observational memory, runEvals, and dataset experiments.
- [Experiments](references/docs-evals-experiments.md) - Run Mastra dataset experiments against registered agents or workflows, apply scorers, compare results, and inspect experiment output in Studio.
- [Gates and verdicts](references/docs-evals-gates-and-verdicts.md) - Define mandatory gates and score thresholds for Mastra evals, compute passed, scored, or failed verdicts, and enforce quality requirements in CI.
- [Multi-turn evals](references/docs-evals-multi-turn.md) - Evaluate Mastra agents across multi-turn conversations by sending sequential inputs on one memory thread and scoring individual turns or the full exchange.
- [Evals](references/docs-evals-overview.md) - Evaluate Mastra agents and workflows with model-graded, rule-based, and programmatic scorers through live evaluations, trace scoring, and Quick Checks.
- [Running scorers in CI](references/docs-evals-running-in-ci.md) - Run Mastra scorer experiments in CI with runEvals, define test cases for agents or workflows, inspect aggregate results, and track quality over time.
- [Agent lifecycle](references/docs-guides-agent-lifecycle.md) - Follow an agent run from input preparation through repeated model and tool calls to the final result, for both regular and durable execution.
- [Authentication and identity](references/docs-guides-authentication-identity.md) - Design secure identity flows for Mastra that protect endpoints and carry trusted user context through agents and tools while enforcing data boundaries.
- [Context engineering](references/docs-guides-context-engineering.md) - Engineer the context Mastra agents receive by combining instructions, inline data, tools, RAG, filesystems, memory, and observational memory.
- [Multi-agent systems](references/docs-guides-multi-agent-systems.md) - Choose a Mastra multi-agent architecture by comparing handoffs, workflows, supervisors, and council patterns for delegation, control, and collaboration.
- [Streaming](references/docs-guides-streaming.md) - Stream incremental responses from Mastra agents and workflows, consume text and structured output, handle events, and integrate with AI SDK interfaces.
- [Agent Controller](references/docs-harness-agent-controller.md) - Build interactive Mastra agent applications with Agent Controller sessions, persistent threads, modes, approvals, subagents, channels, and runtime state.
- [Background tasks](references/docs-harness-background-tasks.md) - Run long-lived Mastra tool calls and subagents as background tasks while streams remain open, with per-call dispositions, cancellation, and completion events.
- [Durable agents](references/docs-harness-durable-agents.md) - Wrap Mastra agents in durable execution so streams and long-running turns survive client disconnects and process restarts across supported runtimes.
- [Goals](references/docs-harness-goals.md) - Set a durable goal for a Mastra agent so an execution loop evaluates progress and continues working until the objective completes or its run budget ends.
- [Harness](references/docs-harness-overview.md) - Use the Mastra harness to start, continue, update, and preserve agent work beyond one request with durable execution, goals, schedules, and signals.
- [Schedules](references/docs-harness-schedules.md) - Schedule Mastra agents with cron expressions, recurring prompts, optional thread delivery, lifecycle hooks, and APIs for managing scheduled runs.
- [Signal providers](references/docs-harness-signal-providers.md) - Build Mastra signal providers that monitor external systems through polling or webhooks and deliver notifications into long-running agent threads.
- [Signals](references/docs-harness-signals.md) - Send real-time messages or contextual data into a Mastra agent thread immediately or queue them for the next turn with configurable signal behavior.
- [Observability](references/docs-mastra-platform-observability.md) - Collect and query hosted traces, logs, metrics, scores, and feedback from Mastra applications with Mastra Platform Observability and local fallback storage.
- [Memory processors](references/docs-memory-memory-processors.md) - Configure Mastra memory processors to filter, trim, transform, and deduplicate messages before they reach the model while managing context limits.
- [Message history](references/docs-memory-message-history.md) - Store and retrieve recent Mastra conversation messages, configure history limits and thread titles, and query threads for chat interfaces.
- [Multi-user threads](references/docs-memory-multi-user-threads.md) - Share one Mastra memory thread across multiple users by preserving speaker identity in messages and combining history with observational or working memory.
- [Observational Memory](references/docs-memory-observational-memory.md) - Configure Mastra Observational Memory to compress long conversations into durable observations while preserving context across threads and sessions.
- [Memory](references/docs-memory-overview.md) - Add memory to Mastra agents with message history, semantic recall, working memory, and observational memory across threads and multi-agent delegation.
- [Semantic recall](references/docs-memory-semantic-recall.md) - Retrieve relevant messages from past Mastra conversations with semantic recall, vector search, embeddings, metadata filters, and configurable storage.
- [Working memory](references/docs-memory-working-memory.md) - Persist user profiles, preferences, and application data with Mastra working memory using resource- or thread-scoped templates and storage adapters.
- [Feedback](references/docs-observability-feedback.md) - Create, list, aggregate, and export human feedback records in Mastra observability, with ratings and comments linked to specific traces and spans.
- [Computer](references/docs-sandbox-computer.md) - Give Mastra agents screenshot, mouse, and keyboard control in supported desktop sandboxes.
- [Filesystem](references/docs-sandbox-filesystem.md) - Give Mastra agents local or remote filesystem access, configure persistent storage and mounts, and work with files through workspace tools.
- [LSP inspection](references/docs-sandbox-lsp.md) - Configure Language Server Protocol support in Mastra workspaces so agents can inspect symbols, definitions, references, diagnostics, and project structure.
- [Sandboxes](references/docs-sandbox-overview.md) - Run Mastra agents in isolated local or remote sandboxes with filesystem access, shell commands, code execution, and optional computer-use tools.
- [Search and indexing](references/docs-sandbox-search.md) - Index filesystem or application content in Mastra workspaces and search it with BM25 keyword, vector semantic, or hybrid retrieval modes.
- [Skills](references/docs-sandbox-skills.md) - Create filesystem-backed Mastra skills with SKILL.md instructions, supporting files, configurable discovery paths, and Agent Skills compatibility.
- [Custom adapters](references/docs-server-custom-adapters.md) - Implement a custom Mastra server adapter for unsupported web frameworks by mapping routes, middleware, request parameters, responses, and streams.
- [Custom API routes](references/docs-server-custom-api-routes.md) - Add custom HTTP endpoints to a Mastra server with schema validation, middleware, authentication, OpenAPI documentation, and control over disconnect behavior.
- [Mastra client](references/docs-server-mastra-client.md) - Use the type-safe Mastra Client SDK from browser applications to call agents, workflows, tools, memory, and server APIs with streaming support.
- [Middleware](references/docs-server-middleware.md) - Add Mastra server middleware for authentication, authorization, CORS, request logging, route blocking, and request-specific context injection.
- [Server](references/docs-server-overview.md) - Configure the Mastra HTTP server to expose agents and workflows through REST APIs with middleware, authentication, streaming, and OpenAI-compatible routes.
- [PubSub](references/docs-server-pubsub.md) - Configure Mastra PubSub event delivery for components, resumable streams, workers, and schedules across one process, multiple processes, or distributed instances.
- [Request context](references/docs-server-request-context.md) - Pass request-specific runtime values through Mastra RequestContext to configure agents, workflows, tools, models, storage, and instructions for each request.
- [Agent skills](references/docs-skills.md) - Attach reusable Agent Skills directly to Mastra agents using inline definitions, filesystem paths, dynamic loaders, and programmatic skill access.
- [Storage](references/docs-storage.md) - Configure Mastra storage to persist memory, workflow state, observability data, evals, schedules, and long-running agent state across restarts.
- [Auth](references/docs-studio-auth.md) - Secure Mastra Studio and API routes with login flows, token forwarding, role-based access control, default roles, and permission-aware UI rendering.
- [Deployment](references/docs-studio-deployment.md) - Deploy Mastra Studio on Mastra platform, alongside your API, or as a static SPA on your own infrastructure or content delivery network.
- [Editor](references/docs-studio-editor.md) - Use Mastra Studio Editor so collaborators can change agent instructions and tools without modifying source code, from draft testing through publication.
- [Observability](references/docs-studio-observability.md) - Monitor Mastra agents, workflows, tools, and model calls in Studio with metrics dashboards, hierarchical traces, and searchable correlated logs.
- [Studio](references/docs-studio-overview.md) - Use Mastra Studio to build, test, and manage agents, workflows, processors, tools, and MCP servers while inspecting traces and runtime behavior.

- [Agents and tools](references/docs-workflows-agents-and-tools.md) - Call Mastra agents and tools from workflow steps, compose them directly with createStep, and choose between execute functions and typed step composition.
- [Control flow](references/docs-workflows-control-flow.md) - Control Mastra workflow execution with sequential steps, parallel branches, conditional logic, loops, nested workflows, mapping, and output merging.
- [Dynamic workflows](references/docs-workflows-dynamic-workflows.md) - Create, persist, update, and execute Mastra workflows from JSON definitions while registering dependencies and managing definitions through APIs.
- [Error handling](references/docs-workflows-error-handling.md) - Handle Mastra workflow failures with retries, result status checks, lifecycle callbacks, conditional branches, step errors, and monitoring in Studio.
- [Human-in-the-loop](references/docs-workflows-human-in-the-loop.md) - Pause Mastra workflows for approvals, reviews, or user input, then resume with supplied data, reject with bail, or support repeated human interactions.
- [Workflows](references/docs-workflows-overview.md) - Build deterministic Mastra workflows with typed steps, agents, tools, branching, parallel execution, loops, suspension, state, and Studio visualization.
- [Scheduled workflows](references/docs-workflows-scheduled-workflows.md) - Run Mastra workflows on one or more cron schedules, inspect trigger history in Studio, and pause or resume scheduled execution at runtime.
- [Snapshots](references/docs-workflows-snapshots.md) - Store and retrieve Mastra workflow snapshots so suspended executions preserve step results and state and can resume reliably across processes.
- [Suspend and resume](references/docs-workflows-suspend-and-resume.md) - Suspend Mastra workflows while waiting for external input, resources, or time, then resume saved runs with data and recover interrupted executions.
- [Time travel](references/docs-workflows-time-travel.md) - Debug Mastra workflows by re-executing from a selected step with new execution context, including nested steps addressed by reference or ID.
- [Workflow state](references/docs-workflows-workflow-state.md) - Share typed global state across Mastra workflow steps, initialize and update values, preserve state through suspension, and pass it into nested workflows.

### Reference

- [Reference: Overview](references/reference.md) - The Reference section provides documentation of Mastra's API, including parameters, types and usage examples.
- [Reference: AcpAgent class](references/reference-acp-acp-agent.md) - The AcpAgent class wraps an Agent Client Protocol (ACP)-compatible coding agent as a Mastra subagent.
- [Reference: createACPTool()](references/reference-acp-create-acp-tool.md) - The createACPTool() function creates a Mastra tool that sends a task string to an Agent Client Protocol (ACP)-compatible coding agent and returns the final ACP response as output.
- [Reference: AgentController](references/reference-agent-controller-agent-controller-class.md) - Use the AgentController class as a shared host for Session instances, then create sessions and manage conversation state, events, and run control.
- [Reference: Session](references/reference-agent-controller-session.md) - Use AgentController Session to manage per-conversation identity, threads, mode, model, run state, grants, and display snapshots within an isolated runtime.
- [Reference: Agent class](references/reference-agents-agent.md) - The Agent class is the foundation for creating AI agents in Mastra. It provides methods for generating responses and streaming interactions.
- [Reference: Channels](references/reference-agents-channels.md) - Channels connect agents to messaging platforms. Configure them via the channels property on the Agent constructor.
- [Reference: createSkill()](references/reference-agents-createSkill.md) - Creates an inline skill that can be passed directly to an agent's skills config without a filesystem or workspace.
- [Reference: DurableAgent](references/reference-agents-durable-agent.md) - DurableAgent wraps an existing Agent with durable execution and resumable streams.
- [Reference: Agent.generate()](references/reference-agents-generate.md) - The .generate() method enables non-streaming response generation from an agent with enhanced capabilities.
- [Reference: Agent.generateLegacy() (Legacy)](references/reference-agents-generateLegacy.md) - The .generateLegacy() method is the legacy version of the agent generation API, used with legacy model adapters to produce text or structured responses.
- [Reference: Agent.getDefaultGenerateOptionsLegacy()](references/reference-agents-getDefaultGenerateOptions.md) - Agents can be configured with default generation options for controlling model behavior, output formatting and tool and workflow calls.
- [Reference: Agent.getDefaultOptions()](references/reference-agents-getDefaultOptions.md) - Agents can be configured with default options for memory usage and output format. Iteration steps can also be configured.
- [Reference: Agent.getDefaultStreamOptionsLegacy()](references/reference-agents-getDefaultStreamOptions.md) - Agents can be configured with default streaming options for memory usage and output format. Iteration steps can also be configured.
- [Reference: Agent.getDescription()](references/reference-agents-getDescription.md) - The .getDescription() method retrieves the description configured for an agent. This method returns a string description that describes the agent's purpose and capabilities.
- [Reference: Agent.getInstructions()](references/reference-agents-getInstructions.md) - The .getInstructions() method retrieves the instructions configured for an agent, resolving them if they're a function.
- [Reference: Agent.getLLM()](references/reference-agents-getLLM.md) - The .getLLM() method retrieves the language model instance configured for an agent, resolving it if it's a function.
- [Reference: Agent.getMemory()](references/reference-agents-getMemory.md) - Use Agent.getMemory() to retrieve the memory system configured for an agent, including request-context resolution when memory is supplied at runtime.
- [Reference: Agent.getMetadata()](references/reference-agents-getMetadata.md) - The .getMetadata() method retrieves the metadata configured for an agent, resolving it if it's a function.
- [Reference: Agent.getModel()](references/reference-agents-getModel.md) - The .getModel() method retrieves the language model configured for an agent, resolving it if it's a function.
- [Reference: .getSkill()](references/reference-agents-getSkill.md) - Retrieves a specific skill by name from the agent's configured skills (both agent-level and workspace skills).
- [Reference: Agent.getTools()](references/reference-agents-getTools.md) - The .getTools() method retrieves the tools configured for an agent, resolving them if they're a function.
- [Reference: Agent.getVoice()](references/reference-agents-getVoice.md) - The .getVoice() method retrieves the voice provider configured for an agent, resolving it if it's a function.
- [Reference: Agent.listAgents()](references/reference-agents-listAgents.md) - The .listAgents() method retrieves the subagents configured for an agent, resolving them if they're a function.
- [Reference: Agent.listScorers()](references/reference-agents-listScorers.md) - The .listScorers() method retrieves the scoring configuration configured for an agent, resolving it if it's a function.
- [Reference: .listSkills()](references/reference-agents-listSkills.md) - Use Agent.listSkills() to return metadata for every configured agent-level and workspace skill, including the names and descriptions available to the agent.

- [Reference: networkRoute()](references/reference-ai-sdk-network-route.md) - Creates a network route handler for streaming network execution using the AI SDK format.

- [Reference: MastraAuthAuth0 class](references/reference-auth-auth0.md) - Configure MastraAuthAuth0 for Auth0 authentication, including access-token validation and authenticated user resolution from request headers.
- [Reference: MastraAuthClerk class](references/reference-auth-clerk.md) - The MastraAuthClerk class provides authentication for Mastra applications using Clerk.
- [Reference: IFGAProvider](references/reference-auth-fga.md) - Implement IFGAProvider to authorize users and system actors against Mastra resources with fine-grained authorization checks and provider-specific policies.

- [Reference: MastraAuthGoogle and MastraRBACGoogle](references/reference-auth-google.md) - The MastraAuthGoogle class provides authentication for Mastra using Google Workspace.
- [Reference: MastraJwtAuth class](references/reference-auth-jwt.md) - The MastraJwtAuth class provides a lightweight authentication mechanism for Mastra using JSON Web Tokens (JWTs).
- [Reference: MastraAuthNeon and MastraRBACNeon](references/reference-auth-neon.md) - API reference for the MastraAuthNeon authentication provider and MastraRBACNeon role-based access control provider.
- [Reference: MastraAuthOkta and MastraRBACOkta](references/reference-auth-okta.md) - Use MastraAuthOkta and MastraRBACOkta to authenticate users with Okta and enforce role-based access control for Mastra application resources.
- [Reference: MastraAuthSupabase class](references/reference-auth-supabase.md) - The MastraAuthSupabase class provides authentication for Mastra using Supabase Auth.
- [Reference: MastraAuthWorkos class](references/reference-auth-workos.md) - Configure MastraAuthWorkos for WorkOS authentication, including access-token validation and authenticated user resolution from requests.
- [Reference: MastraBrowser class](references/reference-browser-mastra-browser.md) - The MastraBrowser class is the abstract base class for browser automation providers.
- [Reference: ChannelProvider](references/reference-channels-channel-provider.md) - ChannelProvider is the interface that platform integrations implement to connect agents to a messaging platform.
- [Reference: Agents API](references/reference-client-js-agents.md) - The Agents API provides methods to interact with Mastra AI agents, including generating responses and streaming interactions.
- [Reference: buildBasePrompt()](references/reference-coding-agent-build-base-prompt.md) - buildBasePrompt() builds the shared base system prompt for a coding agent: the behavioral instructions that make the agent a good coding assistant.
- [Reference: createCodingAgent()](references/reference-coding-agent-create-coding-agent.md) - Use createCodingAgent() to build a coding agent with a local workspace, task signals, network retries, memory integration, and the goal-judge prompt.
- [Reference: Configuration](references/reference-configuration.md) - Configure a Mastra instance with agents, workflows, storage, logging, observability, server options, processors, deployers, and other supported services.
- [Reference: Mastra.addDynamicWorkflow()](references/reference-core-addDynamicWorkflow.md) - Use Mastra.addDynamicWorkflow() to validate, persist, and register a dynamic workflow definition as a live workflow on the current Mastra instance.
- [Reference: Mastra.addDynamicWorkflows()](references/reference-core-addDynamicWorkflows.md) - The .addDynamicWorkflows() method adds a bundle of dynamic workflow definitions that may reference each other.
- [Reference: Mastra.addGateway()](references/reference-core-addGateway.md) - Dynamically adds a gateway to the Mastra instance. Can be used during or after initialization.

- [Reference: Mastra.getEditor()](references/reference-core-getEditor.md) - The .getEditor() method is used to retrieve the editor instance that has been configured on the Mastra instance.
- [Reference: Mastra.getGateway()](references/reference-core-getGateway.md) - Retrieves a gateway by its registration key (the key used when adding the gateway to Mastra).
- [Reference: Mastra.getGatewayById()](references/reference-core-getGatewayById.md) - Use Mastra.getGatewayById() to retrieve a registered model gateway by its unique gateway ID and handle missing gateway registrations.
- [Reference: Mastra.getLogger()](references/reference-core-getLogger.md) - The .getLogger() method is used to retrieve the logger instance that has been configured in the Mastra instance.
- [Reference: Mastra.getMCPServer()](references/reference-core-getMCPServer.md) - The .getMCPServer() method retrieves an MCP server instance by its registry key (the key used when registering the server in the mcpServers configuration).
- [Reference: Mastra.getMCPServerById()](references/reference-core-getMCPServerById.md) - The .getMCPServerById() method retrieves an MCP server instance by its intrinsic id property.
- [Reference: Mastra.getMemory()](references/reference-core-getMemory.md) - The .getMemory() method retrieves a memory instance from the Mastra registry by its key.
- [Reference: getScorer()](references/reference-core-getScorer.md) - The getScorer() method retrieves a specific scorer that was registered with the Mastra instance using its registration key.
- [Reference: getScorerById()](references/reference-core-getScorerById.md) - The getScorerById() method retrieves a scorer by searching for its id property (or name property as a fallback) rather than the registration key.
- [Reference: Mastra.getServer()](references/reference-core-getServer.md) - The .getServer() method is used to retrieve the server configuration that has been configured in the Mastra instance.
- [Reference: Mastra.getStorage()](references/reference-core-getStorage.md) - The .getStorage() method is used to retrieve the storage instance that has been configured in the Mastra instance.
- [Reference: Mastra.getTelemetry()](references/reference-core-getTelemetry.md) - The .getTelemetry() method is used to retrieve the telemetry instance that has been configured in the Mastra instance.
- [Reference: Mastra.getTool()](references/reference-core-getTool.md) - The .getTool() method retrieves a tool from the Mastra-level registry by its registration key.
- [Reference: Mastra.getToolById()](references/reference-core-getToolById.md) - The .getToolById() method first searches the Mastra-level registry for a tool with a matching intrinsic id.
- [Reference: Mastra.getVector()](references/reference-core-getVector.md) - The .getVector() method is used to retrieve a vector store by its name. The method accepts a single string parameter for the vector store's name.
- [Reference: Mastra.getWorkflow()](references/reference-core-getWorkflow.md) - The .getWorkflow() method is used to retrieve a workflow by its registration key. The method provides full TypeScript type inference for workflow input and output schemas.
- [Reference: Mastra.listAgents()](references/reference-core-listAgents.md) - The .listAgents() method is used to retrieve all agents that have been configured in the Mastra instance.
- [Reference: Mastra.listGateways()](references/reference-core-listGateways.md) - Use Mastra.listGateways() to retrieve every registered model gateway as a record indexed by each gateway's registration key.
- [Reference: Mastra.listLogs()](references/reference-core-listLogs.md) - The .listLogs() method is used to retrieve all logs for a specific transport ID. This method requires a configured logger that supports the listLogs operation.
- [Reference: Mastra.listLogsByRunId()](references/reference-core-listLogsByRunId.md) - The .listLogsByRunId() method is used to retrieve logs for a specific run ID and transport ID. This method requires a configured logger that supports the listLogsByRunId operation.
- [Reference: Mastra.listMCPServers()](references/reference-core-listMCPServers.md) - The .listMCPServers() method is used to retrieve all MCP server instances that have been registered in the Mastra instance.
- [Reference: Mastra.listMemory()](references/reference-core-listMemory.md) - The .listMemory() method returns all memory instances registered with the Mastra instance.
- [Reference: listScorers()](references/reference-core-listScorers.md) - The listScorers() method returns all scorers that have been registered with the Mastra instance.
- [Reference: Mastra.listTools()](references/reference-core-listTools.md) - The .listTools() method returns the tools configured on a Mastra instance. The returned record uses Mastra registration keys and tool instances as values.
- [Reference: Mastra.listVectors()](references/reference-core-listVectors.md) - The .listVectors() method is used to retrieve all vector stores that have been configured in the Mastra instance.
- [Reference: Mastra.listWorkflows()](references/reference-core-listWorkflows.md) - The .listWorkflows() method is used to retrieve all workflows that have been configured in the Mastra instance.
- [Reference: Mastra class](references/reference-core-mastra-class.md) - The Mastra class is the central orchestrator in any Mastra application, managing agents, workflows, storage, logging, observability, and more.
- [Reference: MastraModelGateway](references/reference-core-mastra-model-gateway.md) - Extend MastraModelGateway to implement a custom model gateway with provider discovery, model resolution, authentication, and gateway-specific configuration.
- [Reference: Mastra.removeWorkspace()](references/reference-core-removeWorkspace.md) - The .removeWorkspace() method removes a workspace from the Mastra runtime registry. Pass to destroy the workspace before it's removed.
- [Reference: Mastra.setLogger()](references/reference-core-setLogger.md) - The .setLogger() method is used to set the logger for all components (agents, workflows, etc.) in the Mastra instance.
- [Reference: Mastra.setStorage()](references/reference-core-setStorage.md) - The .setStorage() method is used to set the storage instance for the Mastra instance. This method accepts a single MastraCompositeStore parameter.
- [Reference: dataset.addItem()](references/reference-datasets-addItem.md) - Adds a single item to the dataset. Each item has an input and optional ground truth.
- [Reference: dataset.addItems()](references/reference-datasets-addItems.md) - Use dataset.addItems() to add multiple items to a Mastra dataset in one bulk operation, with schema validation and version tracking for the inserted records.
- [Reference: DatasetsManager.compareExperiments()](references/reference-datasets-compareExperiments.md) - Compares two or more experiments, producing per-item and per-scorer comparisons. Requires at least two experiment IDs.

- [Reference: dataset.createExperiment()](references/reference-datasets-createExperiment.md) - Use dataset.createExperiment() to create a caller-driven experiment without starting a run, then submit results and finalize it from your own orchestrator.
- [Reference: Dataset class](references/reference-datasets-dataset.md) - The Dataset class provides methods for item CRUD, versioning, and experiment management on a single dataset.
- [Reference: DatasetsManager](references/reference-datasets-datasets-manager.md) - The DatasetsManager class provides the public API for managing datasets, including CRUD operations and cross-dataset experiment comparisons.
- [Reference: DatasetsManager.delete()](references/reference-datasets-delete.md) - Use DatasetsManager.delete() to remove a dataset by ID together with its items, versions, experiments, and associated stored records.
- [Reference: deleteExperiment()](references/reference-datasets-deleteExperiment.md) - Use dataset.deleteExperiment() or DatasetsManager.deleteExperiment() to delete an experiment together with its results and observability traces.
- [Reference: dataset.deleteItem()](references/reference-datasets-deleteItem.md) - Use dataset.deleteItem() to remove one dataset item by ID and create the corresponding dataset version and history changes.
- [Reference: dataset.deleteItems()](references/reference-datasets-deleteItems.md) - Use dataset.deleteItems() to remove multiple dataset items in one bulk operation and record the resulting dataset version changes.

- [Reference: dataset.getDetails()](references/reference-datasets-getDetails.md) - Retrieves the full dataset record from storage, including metadata, schemas, and version information.
- [Reference: dataset.getExperiment()](references/reference-datasets-getExperiment.md) - Use dataset.getExperiment() to retrieve a specific experiment by ID, including its status, metadata, target, scorer configuration, and result summary.
- [Reference: dataset.getItem()](references/reference-datasets-getItem.md) - Retrieves a single dataset item by ID, optionally at a specific dataset version.
