- [Reference: DatasetsManager.list()](references/reference-datasets-list.md) - Lists datasets with pagination and optional filters. Filters are applied at the storage layer, so callers don't need to post-filter results.
- [Reference: dataset.listExperimentResults()](references/reference-datasets-listExperimentResults.md) - Lists individual item results for a specific experiment with optional filters and pagination. Filters are applied at the storage layer.
- [Reference: dataset.listExperiments()](references/reference-datasets-listExperiments.md) - Lists experiments (runs) for this dataset with optional filters and pagination. Filters are applied at the storage layer, so results are always scoped to the current dataset.
- [Reference: dataset.listItems()](references/reference-datasets-listItems.md) - Lists items in the dataset. When only version is provided, returns a bare DatasetItem[] snapshot of every item at that version.
- [Reference: dataset.listVersions()](references/reference-datasets-listVersions.md) - Use dataset.listVersions() to retrieve a dataset's version history with pagination, including creation timestamps and change metadata for each version.
- [Reference: dataset.purgeItem()](references/reference-datasets-purgeItem.md) - Documentation for the `dataset.purgeItem()` method, which permanently scrubs an item's stored content.
- [Reference: dataset.runExperimentItem()](references/reference-datasets-runExperimentItem.md) - Execute one experiment item server-side by running its target and resolved scorers, then upsert the result keyed by experimentId, itemId, and attempt.
- [Reference: dataset.startExperiment()](references/reference-datasets-startExperiment.md) - Runs an experiment on the dataset and waits for completion. Executes all items against a target (agent, workflow, or scorer) with optional scoring.
- [Reference: dataset.startExperimentAsync()](references/reference-datasets-startExperimentAsync.md) - Starts an experiment asynchronously (fire-and-forget). Returns immediately with the experiment ID and a 'pending' status.
- [Reference: dataset.submitExperimentResult()](references/reference-datasets-submitExperimentResult.md) - Submits (or re-submits) one externally computed item result for a target-less experiment created with createExperiment().
- [Reference: dataset.update()](references/reference-datasets-update.md) - Updates dataset metadata, name, description, and/or schemas. Use Standard JSON Schema (Zod, Valibot, ArkType, etc.) for defining schemas.
- [Reference: dataset.updateExperiment()](references/reference-datasets-updateExperiment.md) - Use dataset.updateExperiment() to rename an experiment or change its description and metadata after it has been created.
- [Reference: dataset.updateItem()](references/reference-datasets-updateItem.md) - Use dataset.updateItem() to change selected fields on an existing dataset item while validating data and preserving dataset version history.
- [Reference: BlobStoreProvider](references/reference-editor-blob-store-provider.md) - BlobStoreProvider is the interface a package implements to register a blob store with MastraEditor.
- [Reference: BrowserProvider](references/reference-editor-browser-provider.md) - BrowserProvider is the interface a package implements to register a browser with MastraEditor.
- [Reference: FilesystemProvider](references/reference-editor-filesystem-provider.md) - FilesystemProvider is the interface a package implements to register a filesystem with MastraEditor.
- [Reference: MastraEditor class](references/reference-editor-mastra-editor.md) - The MastraEditor class sets up the editor system. Pass it to the Mastra constructor to turn on editor features like prompt blocks, agent code override, versioning, and tool providers.
- [Reference: ProcessorProvider](references/reference-editor-processor-provider.md) - ProcessorProvider is the interface a package implements to register a configurable processor with MastraEditor.
- [Reference: Prompt blocks](references/reference-editor-prompt-blocks.md) - Use Editor prompt blocks to define reusable instruction templates, typed values, display conditions, version history, and agent prompt-block APIs.
- [Reference: SandboxProvider](references/reference-editor-sandbox-provider.md) - SandboxProvider is the interface a package implements to register a sandbox with MastraEditor.
- [Reference: StorageBrowserRef](references/reference-editor-storage-browser-ref.md) - StorageBrowserRef is the inline browser configuration attached to a stored agent.
- [Reference: StorageWorkspaceRef](references/reference-editor-storage-workspace-ref.md) - StorageWorkspaceRef is the discriminated union used to attach a workspace to a stored agent.
- [Reference: Tool configuration](references/reference-editor-tools.md) - Configure Editor agent tools from Mastra, MCP, workspace, and provider sources, including descriptions, display conditions, and resolution order.
- [Reference: Versioning](references/reference-editor-versioning.md) - Editor versions stored agents and prompt blocks. Database-backed resources use draft and publish operations.
- [Reference: Answer relevancy scorer](references/reference-evals-answer-relevancy.md) - Use createAnswerRelevancyScorer() to evaluate how directly an LLM response addresses the input query, with configurable model and scoring options.
- [Reference: Answer similarity scorer](references/reference-evals-answer-similarity.md) - The createAnswerSimilarityScorer() function creates a scorer that evaluates how similar an agent's output is to a ground truth answer.
- [Reference: Bias scorer](references/reference-evals-bias.md) - Use createBiasScorer() to evaluate LLM output for gender, political, racial, ethnic, geographic, and other forms of bias with an LLM judge.
- [Reference: Completeness scorer](references/reference-evals-completeness.md) - The createCompletenessScorer() function evaluates how thoroughly an LLM's output covers the key elements present in the input.
- [Reference: Content similarity scorer](references/reference-evals-content-similarity.md) - The createContentSimilarityScorer() function measures the textual similarity between two strings, providing a score that indicates how closely they match.
- [Reference: Context precision scorer](references/reference-evals-context-precision.md) - The createContextPrecisionScorer() function creates a scorer that evaluates how relevant and well-positioned retrieved context pieces are for generating expected outputs.
- [Reference: Context recall scorer](references/reference-evals-context-recall.md) - The createContextRecallScorer() function creates a scorer that evaluates how well retrieved context covers the claims in a ground-truth reference answer.
- [Reference: createScorer](references/reference-evals-create-scorer.md) - Mastra provides a unified createScorer factory that allows you to define custom scorers for evaluating input/output pairs.
- [Reference: Faithfulness scorer](references/reference-evals-faithfulness.md) - The createFaithfulnessScorer() function evaluates how factually accurate an LLM's output is compared to the provided context.
- [Reference: filterRun()](references/reference-evals-filter-run.md) - Creates a prepareRun function from declarative options. Pass the result to createScorer() to filter messages and limit context size.
- [Reference: Hallucination scorer](references/reference-evals-hallucination.md) - The createHallucinationScorer() function evaluates whether an LLM generates factually correct information by comparing its output against the provided context.
- [Reference: Keyword coverage scorer](references/reference-evals-keyword-coverage.md) - The createKeywordCoverageScorer() function evaluates how well an LLM's output covers the important keywords from the input.
- [Reference: MastraScorer](references/reference-evals-mastra-scorer.md) - Use the MastraScorer base class to understand the shared scorer contract, lifecycle, run inputs, outputs, tracing behavior, and custom scorer implementation.
- [Reference: runEvals](references/reference-evals-run-evals.md) - The runEvals function enables batch evaluation of agents and workflows by running multiple test cases against scorers concurrently.
- [Reference: Scorer utils](references/reference-evals-scorer-utils.md) - Mastra provides utility functions to help extract and process data from scorer run inputs and outputs. These utilities are particularly useful in the preprocess step of custom scorers.
- [Reference: Summarization scorer](references/reference-evals-summarization.md) - Use createSummarizationScorer() to evaluate whether a summary is supported by its source text and preserves the source's important information.
- [Reference: Textual difference scorer](references/reference-evals-textual-difference.md) - The createTextualDifferenceScorer() function uses sequence matching to measure the textual differences between two strings.
- [Reference: Tone consistency scorer](references/reference-evals-tone-consistency.md) - The createToneScorer() function evaluates the text's emotional tone and sentiment consistency.
- [Reference: Toxicity scorer](references/reference-evals-toxicity.md) - The createToxicityScorer() function evaluates whether an LLM's output contains racist, biased, or toxic elements.
- [Reference: Trajectory accuracy scorers](references/reference-evals-trajectory-accuracy.md) - Use trajectory accuracy scorers to compare an agent or workflow's tool and step sequence with an expected execution path or ordered trajectory.
- [config.ts](references/reference-file-based-agents-config.md) - An agent's config.ts sets its model and runtime options. Use it for options that belong to the Agent itself, while sibling files provide instructions, tools, skills, et cetera.
- [Instructions](references/reference-file-based-agents-instructions.md) - An agent's instructions hold its always-on system prompt: the model reads it on every turn. Use them to define the agent's identity, tone, role, and standing rules.
- [Logger](references/reference-file-based-agents-logger.md) - Mastra sets the project's logger from a logger.ts file directly under src/mastra/.
- [Memory](references/reference-file-based-agents-memory.md) - A file-based agent gets memory from a memory.ts file that default-exports a Memory instance.
- [Observability](references/reference-file-based-agents-observability.md) - Mastra configures observability from an observability.ts file directly under src/mastra/.
- [Processors](references/reference-file-based-agents-processors.md) - Add input and output processors to file-based agents under processors/input and processors/output, with module exports discovered during build.
- [Schedules](references/reference-file-based-agents-schedules.md) - A file-based agent discovers schedules from its schedules/ directory. Each file declares one recurring task: a cron expression plus what the agent should do when it fires.
- [Scorers](references/reference-file-based-agents-scorers.md) - A file-based agent discovers scorers from its scorers/ directory. Use this page for the file-based convention; use the scorers guide for built-in scorers, custom scorers, and sampling.
- [Server](references/reference-file-based-agents-server.md) - Mastra configures its HTTP server from a server.ts file directly under src/mastra/.
- [Skills](references/reference-file-based-agents-skills.md) - A file-based agent discovers skills from its skills/ directory and bundles them at build time.
- [Storage](references/reference-file-based-agents-storage.md) - Mastra sets the project's default storage from a storage.ts file directly under src/mastra/.
- [Studio](references/reference-file-based-agents-studio.md) - Configure Mastra Studio by exporting Studio options from src/mastra/studio.ts in a file-based Mastra project.
- [Subagents](references/reference-file-based-agents-subagents.md) - A file-based agent can declare subagents, specialist child agents it delegates to.
- [Tools](references/reference-file-based-agents-tools.md) - A file-based agent discovers tools from .ts and .js files directly under its tools/ directory.
- [Workflows](references/reference-file-based-agents-workflows.md) - Mastra discovers project-level workflows from .ts and .js files under src/mastra/workflows/.
- [Workspace](references/reference-file-based-agents-workspace.md) - A workspace assembles capabilities such as filesystem access and command execution. The configured backends determine which tools are available.
- [Reference: PinoLogger](references/reference-logging-pino-logger.md) - A Logger instance is created using new PinoLogger() and provides methods to record events at severity levels.
- [Manual install](references/reference-manual-install.md) - Create a runnable Mastra project without the CLI by installing the required packages and configuring TypeScript, then define an agent and Mastra entry point.
- [Reference: Memory.deleteMessages()](references/reference-memory-deleteMessages.md) - Use Memory.deleteMessages() to remove multiple messages by ID from a conversation thread and its configured storage provider.
- [Reference: Memory class](references/reference-memory-memory-class.md) - The Memory class provides a reliable system for managing conversation history and thread-based message storage in Mastra.
- [Reference: Observational Memory](references/reference-memory-observational-memory.md) - Observational Memory (OM) is Mastra's memory system for long-context agentic memory. An Observer watches conversations and creates observations.
- [Reference: SerializedMemoryConfig](references/reference-memory-serialized-memory-config.md) - SerializedMemoryConfig is the JSON-serializable subset of Memory configuration that lives on a stored agent record.
- [Reference: Memory.settled()](references/reference-memory-settled.md) - Use Memory.settled() to wait for asynchronous memory work, including working-memory updates and observational memory, before closing storage.
- [Migration: AgentNetwork to .network()](references/reference-migrations-agentnetwork.md) - Migrate deprecated AgentNetwork usage to supervisor agents and the standard Agent.generate() or Agent.stream() APIs in current Mastra releases.
- [Migration: AI SDK v4 to v5](references/reference-migrations-ai-sdk-v4-to-v5.md) - Follow the official AI SDK v5 Migration Guide for all AI SDK core breaking changes, package updates, and API changes.
- [Migrate from Mastra Cloud](references/reference-migrations-mastra-cloud.md) - The Mastra platform replaces Mastra Cloud with separate Studio and Server products, CLI-driven deploys, and a new observability system.
- [Migration: .network() to supervisor agents](references/reference-migrations-network-to-supervisor.md) - Supervisor agents using Agent.stream() and Agent.generate() are the recommended approach for coordinating multiple agents, replacing the older .network() API.
- [Agent class](references/reference-migrations-upgrade-to-v1-agent.md) - The Agent class has been updated with reorganized voice methods and property access patterns, plus streamlined streaming APIs.
- [Evals and scorers](references/reference-migrations-upgrade-to-v1-evals.md) - The evaluation API has been consolidated on the new scorers system with updated naming conventions and configuration requirements.
- [Mastra class](references/reference-migrations-upgrade-to-v1-mastra.md) - The Mastra class has been restructured to restrict top-level imports and replace direct property access with getter methods.
- [Memory](references/reference-migrations-upgrade-to-v1-memory.md) - Memory configuration now requires explicit parameters, and default settings have been updated for better performance and predictability.
- [Overview](references/reference-migrations-upgrade-to-v1-overview.md) - Mastra v1 was released in January 2026. We recommend starting any new projects with Mastra v1, or upgrading your existing project to continue receiving updates and support.
- [Processors](references/reference-migrations-upgrade-to-v1-processors.md) - Processor interfaces have been updated to use consistent naming patterns and database message types.
- [Storage](references/reference-migrations-upgrade-to-v1-storage.md) - Storage APIs have been standardized with consistent pagination and naming patterns across all methods.
- [Tools](references/reference-migrations-upgrade-to-v1-tools.md) - Tool execution signatures have been updated to use separate input and context parameters with reorganized context properties.
- [Tracing](references/reference-migrations-upgrade-to-v1-tracing.md) - The observability system has been restructured in v1 with a dedicated @mastra/observability package.
- [Vectors](references/reference-migrations-upgrade-to-v1-vectors.md) - Vector store constructors now require an id property, and vector store methods have been renamed to follow consistent naming conventions.
- [Voice](references/reference-migrations-upgrade-to-v1-voice.md) - Voice packages have been renamed from speech to voice with updated class names and API methods.
- [Workflows](references/reference-migrations-upgrade-to-v1-workflows.md) - Migrate workflow code to Mastra v1 by replacing renamed workflow lookup APIs and updating affected workflow method calls.
- [Migration: VNext to standard APIs](references/reference-migrations-vnext-to-standard-apis.md) - Migrate from VNext methods to Mastra's standard agent generation and streaming APIs, including renamed options, result types, and compatibility changes.
- [Reference: Feedback](references/reference-observability-feedback.md) - Feedback APIs store and query human-in-the-loop observability signals such as ratings, thumbs, comments, and corrections.
- [Reference: Metric queries](references/reference-observability-metrics-queries.md) - Metric queries read raw and aggregated metric data from the observability storage domain. For exporter and storage setup, see the Metrics overview.
- [Reference: DatadogBridge](references/reference-observability-tracing-bridges-datadog.md) - Configure DatadogBridge for bidirectional context propagation between Mastra tracing and Datadog APM spans, including trace and parent IDs.
- [Reference: OtelBridge](references/reference-observability-tracing-bridges-otel.md) - Enables bidirectional integration between Mastra tracing and OpenTelemetry infrastructure. Creates native OTEL spans for Mastra operations and inherits context from active OTEL spans.
- [Reference: Configuration](references/reference-observability-tracing-configuration.md) - Configure Mastra observability instances, tracing exporters, sampling, propagation, span filters, and the global observability registry.
- [Reference: ConsoleExporter](references/reference-observability-tracing-exporters-console-exporter.md) - Configure ConsoleExporter to print Mastra trace events, spans, attributes, and lifecycle updates to the console for local debugging.
- [Reference: DatadogExporter](references/reference-observability-tracing-exporters-datadog.md) - Configure DatadogExporter to send Mastra traces into Datadog LLM Observability, supporting application monitoring and analysis of spans and AI performance.
- [Reference: Tracing](references/reference-observability-tracing-instances.md) - Use ObservabilityInstance and its default implementation to create, manage, flush, and shut down Mastra tracing instances and exporters.
- [Reference: Interfaces](references/reference-observability-tracing-interfaces.md) - Use Mastra tracing interfaces to type spans, attributes, exporters, samplers, propagation context, and observability event payloads.
- [Reference: Span filtering](references/reference-observability-tracing-span-filtering.md) - Span filtering controls which spans are exported from an observability config. Use it to reduce noise or lower per-span costs.
- [Reference: Spans](references/reference-observability-tracing-spans.md) - Span interface, used internally for tracing. Extends BaseSpan with lifecycle methods and properties.
- [Reference: AgentsMDInjector](references/reference-processors-agents-md-injector.md) - Load directory instructions from completed tool calls and configure reader-owned path identities for deduplication.
- [Reference: BatchPartsProcessor](references/reference-processors-batch-parts-processor.md) - The BatchPartsProcessor is an output processor that batches multiple stream parts together to reduce the frequency of emissions during streaming.
- [Reference: LanguageDetector](references/reference-processors-language-detector.md) - The LanguageDetector is an input processor that identifies the language of input text and optionally translates it to a target language for consistent processing.
- [Reference: MessageHistory](references/reference-processors-message-history-processor.md) - The MessageHistory is a hybrid processor that handles both retrieval and persistence of message history.
- [Reference: ModerationProcessor](references/reference-processors-moderation-processor.md) - Use ModerationProcessor for LLM-based input and output moderation across configurable content categories, thresholds, strategies, and model settings.
- [Reference: PIIDetector](references/reference-processors-pii-detector.md) - The PIIDetector is a hybrid processor that can be used for both input and output processing to detect and redact personally identifiable information (PII) for privacy compliance.
- [Reference: PrefillErrorHandler](references/reference-processors-prefill-error-handler.md) - The PrefillErrorHandler is an error processor that handles assistant-response prefill errors.
- [Reference: Processor interface](references/reference-processors-processor-interface.md) - The Processor interface defines the contract for all processors in Mastra. Processors can implement one or more methods to handle different stages of the agent execution pipeline.
- [Reference: PromptInjectionDetector](references/reference-processors-prompt-injection-detector.md) - Use PromptInjectionDetector to block prompt injection, jailbreak, and system-manipulation attempts before messages reach the language model.
- [Reference: ProviderHistoryCompat](references/reference-processors-provider-history-compat.md) - The ProviderHistoryCompat processor handles provider-specific history incompatibilities.
- [Reference: RegexFilterProcessor](references/reference-processors-regex-filter-processor.md) - The RegexFilterProcessor uses regex pattern matching to filter, redact, or block content in agent messages.
- [Reference: ResponseCache](references/reference-processors-response-cache.md) - ResponseCache is an input processor that caches LLM responses on the request/response boundary inside the agentic loop.
- [Reference: SemanticRecall](references/reference-processors-semantic-recall-processor.md) - The SemanticRecall is a hybrid processor that enables semantic search over conversation history using vector embeddings.
- [Reference: SkillSearchProcessor](references/reference-processors-skill-search-processor.md) - The SkillSearchProcessor is an input processor that enables on-demand skill discovery and loading.
- [Reference: StreamErrorRetryProcessor](references/reference-processors-stream-error-retry-processor.md) - StreamErrorRetryProcessor is an error processor that retries transient LLM API and stream failures.
- [Reference: SystemPromptScrubber](references/reference-processors-system-prompt-scrubber.md) - The SystemPromptScrubber is an output processor that detects and handles system prompts, instructions, and other revealing information that could introduce security vulnerabilities.
- [Reference: TokenCostControl](references/reference-processors-token-cost-control.md) - The TokenCostControl enforces monetary cost limits across the agentic loop, blocking or warning when a configurable cost threshold is exceeded.
- [Reference: TokenLimiterProcessor](references/reference-processors-token-limiter-processor.md) - Use TokenLimiterProcessor to constrain message tokens during input, per-step input, or output processing with configurable limits and strategies.
- [Reference: ToolCallFilter](references/reference-processors-tool-call-filter.md) - The ToolCallFilter is an input processor that filters out tool calls and their results from the prompt sent to the model.
- [Reference: ToolSearchProcessor](references/reference-processors-tool-search-processor.md) - The ToolSearchProcessor is an input processor that enables runtime-defined tool discovery and loading.
- [Reference: UnicodeNormalizer](references/reference-processors-unicode-normalizer.md) - Use UnicodeNormalizer to standardize input text into a selected Unicode form and remove problematic characters before messages reach the language model.
- [Reference: WorkingMemory](references/reference-processors-working-memory-processor.md) - The WorkingMemory is an input processor that injects working memory data as a system message.
- [Project structure](references/reference-project-structure.md) - Your new Mastra project, created with the create mastra command, comes with a predefined set of files and folders to help you get started.
- [Reference: PubSub](references/reference-pubsub-base.md) - Extend the PubSub abstract class to implement Mastra event publishing, subscriptions, message delivery, and provider lifecycle behavior.
- [Reference: CachingPubSub](references/reference-pubsub-caching-pubsub.md) - CachingPubSub wraps any PubSub implementation and adds event caching and replay.
- [Reference: EventEmitterPubSub](references/reference-pubsub-event-emitter.md) - EventEmitterPubSub is the default PubSub implementation. It delivers events in-process using a Node.js EventEmitter, so it works without any external service.
- [Reference: GoogleCloudPubSub](references/reference-pubsub-google-cloud-pubsub.md) - Configure GoogleCloudPubSub to deliver Mastra events through Google Cloud Pub/Sub topics and subscriptions in distributed deployments.
- [Reference: LeaseProvider](references/reference-pubsub-lease-provider.md) - LeaseProvider is the distributed leasing contract, separate from event delivery (PubSub).
- [Reference: RedisStreamsPubSub](references/reference-pubsub-redis-streams.md) - RedisStreamsPubSub is a PubSub implementation backed by Redis Streams. It delivers events across processes and hosts, with persistence, consumer groups, and redelivery on failure.
- [Reference: UnixSocketPubSub](references/reference-pubsub-unix-socket-pubsub.md) - UnixSocketPubSub is a PubSub implementation that delivers events across processes on a single host using a Unix domain socket.
- [Reference: ValkeyStreamsPubSub](references/reference-pubsub-valkey-streams.md) - ValkeyStreamsPubSub is a PubSub and LeaseProvider implementation backed by Valkey Streams through Valkey GLIDE.
- [Chunking and embedding documents](references/reference-rag-chunking-and-embedding.md) - Chunk documents with MDocument, generate embeddings through the AI SDK, and prepare text and metadata for vector storage and RAG retrieval.
- [Reference: DatabaseConfig](references/reference-rag-database-config.md) - The DatabaseConfig type allows you to specify database-specific configurations when using vector query tools.
- [Reference: Embed](references/reference-rag-embeddings.md) - Mastra uses the AI SDK's embed and embedMany functions to generate vector embeddings for text inputs, enabling similarity search and RAG workflows.
- [GraphRAG](references/reference-rag-graph-rag-guide.md) - Graph-based retrieval enhances traditional vector search by following relationships between chunks of information.
- [RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) in Mastra](references/reference-rag-overview.md) - RAG in Mastra helps you enhance LLM outputs by incorporating relevant context from your own data sources, improving accuracy and grounding responses in real information.
- [Retrieval, semantic search, reranking](references/reference-rag-retrieval.md) - After storing embeddings, you need to retrieve relevant chunks to answer user queries.
- [Storing embeddings in a vector database](references/reference-rag-vector-databases.md) - After generating embeddings, you need to store them in a database that supports vector similarity search.
- [Reference: mastra.schedules](references/reference-schedules-overview.md) - mastra.schedules is the CRUD service for persisted cron schedules. Use it to create, list, update, pause, resume, manually run, and delete schedules for agents or workflows.
- [Reference: MastraServer](references/reference-server-mastra-server.md) - The MastraServer abstract class is the base for all server adapters. Extend this class to create adapters for frameworks other than Hono or Express.
- [Reference: registerApiRoute()](references/reference-server-register-api-route.md) - The registerApiRoute() function creates custom HTTP routes that integrate with the Mastra server. Routes can include OpenAPI metadata to appear in the Swagger UI documentation.
- [Reference: createNotificationInboxTool()](references/reference-signals-create-notification-inbox-tool.md) - createNotificationInboxTool() creates a Mastra tool that lets an agent inspect and manage notification inbox records for the current thread.
- [Reference: SignalProvider](references/reference-signals-signal-provider.md) - Extend SignalProvider to monitor APIs, webhooks, or event streams and push external notifications into subscribed Mastra agent threads.
- [Reference: TaskSignalProvider](references/reference-signals-task-signal-provider.md) - Register TaskSignalProvider to add task_write, task_update, task_complete, and task_check tools with TaskStateProcessor-backed durable task state.
- [Reference: WebhookSignalProvider](references/reference-signals-webhook-signal-provider.md) - Use WebhookSignalProvider for push-based signals that route incoming webhook payloads to subscribed agent threads and pending signal handlers.
- [Reference: Composite storage](references/reference-storage-composite.md) - MastraCompositeStore can compose storage domains from different providers. Use it when you need different databases for different purposes.
- [Reference: Storage](references/reference-storage-overview.md) - Mastra storage is organized into domains. Each domain owns a set of tables or collections.
- [Reference: Storage retention (prune)](references/reference-storage-retention.md) - prune() deletes rows. It caps growth and is safe to run against large tables (batched, bounded, resumable, cancellable).
- [Reference: MastraModelOutput](references/reference-streaming-agents-MastraModelOutput.md) - The MastraModelOutput class is returned by .stream() and provides both streaming and promise-based access to model outputs.
- [Reference: Agent.streamLegacy() (Legacy)](references/reference-streaming-agents-streamLegacy.md) - The .streamLegacy() method is the legacy version of the agent streaming API, used for real-time streaming of responses from V1 model agents.
- [Reference: Agent.streamUntilIdle()](references/reference-streaming-agents-streamUntilIdle.md) - streamUntilIdle() streams an agent's response and keeps the stream open until every background task dispatched during the run completes.
- [Reference: ChunkType](references/reference-streaming-ChunkType.md) - The ChunkType type defines the mastra format of stream chunks that can be emitted during streaming responses from agents.
- [Reference: smoothStream()](references/reference-streaming-smoothStream.md) - smoothStream() creates an experimental transform stream that buffers text and reasoning deltas before emitting them in consistent chunks.
- [Reference: Run.observeStream()](references/reference-streaming-workflows-observeStream.md) - Use Run.observeStream() to reopen a ReadableStream for an active workflow run and continue observing events after the original stream is unavailable.
- [Reference: Run.resumeStream()](references/reference-streaming-workflows-resumeStream.md) - The .resumeStream() method resumes a suspended workflow run with new data, allowing you to continue execution from a specific step and to observe the stream of events.
- [Reference: Run.stream()](references/reference-streaming-workflows-stream.md) - The .stream() method enables real-time streaming of responses from a workflow. It returns a ReadableStream of events directly.
- [Reference: Run.timeTravelStream()](references/reference-streaming-workflows-timeTravelStream.md) - The .timeTravelStream() method re-executes a workflow starting from any specific step with streaming events.
- [Reference: Templates](references/reference-templates-overview.md) - This reference explains how to use existing Mastra templates and create your own. It also covers contributing templates to the community ecosystem.
- [Reference: askUserTool](references/reference-tools-ask-user-tool.md) - A built-in, agent-agnostic tool that asks the user a question and waits for their response. The tool supports free-text questions, single-select prompts, and multi-select prompts.
- [Reference: createBedrockKBTool()](references/reference-tools-bedrock-kb-tool.md) - The createBedrockKBTool() function creates a tool that retrieves relevant documents from an Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base.
- [Reference: createCodeMode()](references/reference-tools-create-code-mode.md) - The createCodeMode() function returns a tool and generated instructions that let an agent run multi-tool computations as one TypeScript function.
- [Reference: createTool()](references/reference-tools-create-tool.md) - The createTool() function is used to define custom tools that your Mastra agents can execute.
- [Reference: createGraphRAGTool()](references/reference-tools-graph-rag-tool.md) - Use createGraphRAGTool() to build semantic relationships between document chunks and retrieve connected context for graph-based RAG queries.
- [Reference: MCPClient](references/reference-tools-mcp-client.md) - The MCPClient class provides a way to manage multiple MCP server connections and their tools in a Mastra application.
- [Reference: MCPServer](references/reference-tools-mcp-server.md) - The MCPServer class provides the functionality to expose your existing Mastra tools and Agents as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.
- [Reference: submitPlanTool](references/reference-tools-submit-plan-tool.md) - A built-in, agent-agnostic tool that submits an implementation plan for user review. The agent writes a plan to a markdown file and passes the file path to this tool.
- [Reference: Task tools](references/reference-tools-task-tools.md) - Four built-in, agent-agnostic tools that manage a structured task list for an agent run.
- [Reference: createVectorQueryTool()](references/reference-tools-vector-query-tool.md) - The createVectorQueryTool() function creates a tool for semantic search over vector stores.
- [Reference: libSQL vector store](references/reference-vectors-libsql.md) - Configure LibSQLVector for similarity search and metadata filtering with local libSQL, SQLite-compatible vector extensions, or Turso databases.
- [Reference: MongoDB vector store](references/reference-vectors-mongodb.md) - The MongoDBVector class provides vector search using MongoDB Vector Search. It enables efficient similarity search and metadata filtering within your MongoDB collections.
- [Reference: OracleDB vector store](references/reference-vectors-oracledb.md) - OracleVector stores embeddings in Oracle Database VECTOR columns and exposes them through Mastra's vector interface.
- [Reference: PG vector store](references/reference-vectors-pg.md) - The PgVector class provides vector search using PostgreSQL with pgvector extension. It provides reliable vector similarity search capabilities within your existing PostgreSQL database.
- [Reference: Upstash vector store](references/reference-vectors-upstash.md) - Configure UpstashVector for serverless similarity and hybrid search, metadata filtering, index management, and vector operations with Upstash Vector.
- [Reference: CompositeVoice](references/reference-voice-composite-voice.md) - The CompositeVoice class allows you to combine different voice providers for text-to-speech and speech-to-text operations.
- [Reference: MastraVoice](references/reference-voice-mastra-voice.md) - The MastraVoice class is an abstract base class that defines the core interface for voice services in Mastra.
- [Voice in Mastra](references/reference-voice-overview.md) - Use Mastra Voice for text-to-speech, speech-to-text, and real-time speech-to-speech interactions through a unified provider interface.
- [Speech-to-Speech capabilities in Mastra](references/reference-voice-speech-to-speech.md) - Speech-to-Speech (STS) in Mastra provides a standardized interface for real-time interactions across multiple providers.
- [Speech-to-Text (STT)](references/reference-voice-speech-to-text.md) - Speech-to-Text (STT) in Mastra provides a standardized interface for converting audio input into text across multiple service providers.
- [Text-to-Speech (TTS)](references/reference-voice-text-to-speech.md) - Text-to-Speech (TTS) in Mastra offers a unified API for synthesizing spoken audio from text using providers.
- [Reference: voice.addInstructions()](references/reference-voice-voice.addInstructions.md) - The addInstructions() method equips a voice provider with instructions that guide the model's behavior during real-time interactions.
- [Reference: voice.addTools()](references/reference-voice-voice.addTools.md) - The addTools() method equips a voice provider with tools (functions) that the model can call during real-time interactions.
- [Reference: voice.connect()](references/reference-voice-voice.connect.md) - The connect() method establishes a WebSocket or WebRTC connection for real-time speech-to-speech communication.
- [Reference: Voice events](references/reference-voice-voice.events.md) - Handle events emitted by real-time Mastra voice providers for connection state, audio, transcripts, responses, errors, and tool calls.
- [Reference: voice.listen()](references/reference-voice-voice.listen.md) - The listen() method is a core function available in all Mastra voice providers that converts speech to text.
- [Reference: voice.on()](references/reference-voice-voice.on.md) - Use voice.on() to register listeners for real-time voice events, including audio, transcripts, responses, errors, and connection changes.
- [Reference: voice.speak()](references/reference-voice-voice.speak.md) - The speak() method is a core function available in all Mastra voice providers that converts text to speech.
- [Reference: Workers](references/reference-workers-overview.md) - Use Mastra workers as background processing units for workflow orchestration, cron scheduling, durable execution, and asynchronous tasks.
- [Reference: Dynamic workflow definition](references/reference-workflows-dynamic-workflow-definition.md) - A dynamic workflow definition is a JSON-compatible DynamicWorkflowGraph accepted by Mastra.addDynamicWorkflow(), the stored-workflow server routes, and the Client SDK workflows API.
- [Reference: Run class](references/reference-workflows-run.md) - The Run class represents a workflow execution instance, providing methods to start, resume, stream, and monitor workflow execution.
- [Reference: Run.cancel()](references/reference-workflows-run-methods-cancel.md) - The .cancel() method cancels a workflow run, stopping execution and cleaning up resources.
- [Reference: Run.restart()](references/reference-workflows-run-methods-restart.md) - The .restart() method restarts an active workflow run that lost connection to the server, allowing you to continue execution from the moment it lost connection (the last active step).
- [Reference: Run.resume()](references/reference-workflows-run-methods-resume.md) - The .resume() method resumes a suspended workflow run with new data, allowing you to continue execution from a specific step.
- [Reference: Run.start()](references/reference-workflows-run-methods-start.md) - The .start() method starts a workflow run with input data, allowing you to execute the workflow from the beginning.
- [Reference: Run.startAsync()](references/reference-workflows-run-methods-startAsync.md) - The .startAsync() method starts a workflow run without waiting for completion. It returns immediately with the runId, allowing the workflow to execute in the background.
- [Reference: Run.timeTravel()](references/reference-workflows-run-methods-timeTravel.md) - The .timeTravel() method re-executes a workflow starting from any specific step, using either stored snapshot data or custom context you provide.
- [Reference: Step class](references/reference-workflows-step.md) - The Step class defines individual units of work within a workflow, encapsulating execution logic, data validation, and input/output handling.
- [Reference: Workflow class](references/reference-workflows-workflow.md) - The Workflow class enables you to create state machines for complex sequences of operations with conditional branching and data validation.
- [Reference: Workflow.agent()](references/reference-workflows-workflow-methods-agent.md) - Use Workflow.agent() to add a portable agent step with prompt input, text or structured output, runtime agent lookup, retries, scorers, and metadata.
- [Reference: Workflow.branch()](references/reference-workflows-workflow-methods-branch.md) - The .branch() method creates conditional branches between workflow steps, allowing for different paths to be taken based on the result of a previous step.
- [Reference: Workflow.commit()](references/reference-workflows-workflow-methods-commit.md) - Use Workflow.commit() to validate and finalize a workflow definition, returning a committed graph that's ready to create runs.
- [Reference: Workflow.createRun()](references/reference-workflows-workflow-methods-create-run.md) - The .createRun() method creates a new workflow run instance, allowing you to execute the workflow with specific input data.
- [Reference: Workflow.dountil()](references/reference-workflows-workflow-methods-dountil.md) - The .dountil() method executes a step until a condition is met. It always runs the step at least once before evaluating the condition.
- [Reference: Workflow.dowhile()](references/reference-workflows-workflow-methods-dowhile.md) - The .dowhile() method executes a step while a condition is met. It always runs the step at least once before evaluating the condition.
- [Reference: Workflow.foreach()](references/reference-workflows-workflow-methods-foreach.md) - The .foreach() method creates a loop that executes a step for each item in an array. It always returns an array containing the output from each iteration, preserving the original order.
- [Reference: Workflow.map()](references/reference-workflows-workflow-methods-map.md) - The .map() method maps output data from a previous step to the input of a subsequent step, allowing you to transform data between steps.
- [Reference: Workflow.parallel()](references/reference-workflows-workflow-methods-parallel.md) - Use Workflow.parallel() to run multiple steps concurrently and wait for every branch before passing their combined results to later workflow steps.
- [Reference: Workflow.sleep()](references/reference-workflows-workflow-methods-sleep.md) - The .sleep() method pauses execution for a specified number of milliseconds. It accepts either a static number or a callback function for runtime-defined delays.
- [Reference: Workflow.sleepUntil()](references/reference-workflows-workflow-methods-sleepUntil.md) - Use Workflow.sleepUntil() to pause workflow execution until a specified date and resume the run through the configured execution engine.
- [Reference: Workflow.then()](references/reference-workflows-workflow-methods-then.md) - The .then() method creates a sequential dependency between workflow steps, ensuring steps execute in a specific order.
- [Reference: Workflow.tool()](references/reference-workflows-workflow-methods-tool.md) - The .tool() method adds a tool as a declarative step. The tool's own input and output schemas apply, so the previous step's output must satisfy the tool's input schema.
- [Reference: Workflow state reader](references/reference-workflows-workflow-state-reader.md) - Use workflow state reader helpers to inspect WorkflowState status, step inputs and outputs, suspended paths, and resume labels without parsing snapshots.
- [Reference: WorkspaceFilesystem](references/reference-workspace-filesystem.md) - The WorkspaceFilesystem interface defines how workspaces interact with file storage.
- [Reference: LocalFilesystem](references/reference-workspace-local-filesystem.md) - Stores files in a directory on the local filesystem. For interface details, see WorkspaceFilesystem Interface.
- [Reference: LocalSandbox](references/reference-workspace-local-sandbox.md) - Executes commands on the local system. For interface details, see WorkspaceSandbox interface.
- [Reference: SandboxProcessManager](references/reference-workspace-process-manager.md) - Abstract base class for managing background processes in sandboxes. Provides methods to spawn processes, list them, get handles by PID, and kill them.
- [Reference: WorkspaceSandbox](references/reference-workspace-sandbox.md) - The WorkspaceSandbox interface defines how workspaces execute commands and manage background processes.
- [Reference: Workspace class](references/reference-workspace-workspace-class.md) - The Workspace class combines a filesystem and sandbox to provide agents with file storage and command execution capabilities.
